correctness.rationale: For this labelled GP(6,2), exhaustive shortest-distance comparisons with and without each edge reproduce all three representative witness tables, of sizes 6, 7 and 3. Rotation covers the graph. Spoke and inner-edge witnesses force an endpoint of their respective edges; conversely, the tables witness every edge under the spoke and triangle conditions. For each parity independently, at most one spoke can be outer-only, giving (z+z²)^3+3z(z+z²)^2. Taking the inner vertex whenever available yields a size-six subset satisfying the same criterion, so there are no other inclusion-minimal sets. Any valid one-token exchange switches endpoints at one spoke, and is thus also a slide; for each parity the three nonempty outer-index states are adjacent only to the empty state. A fresh replay tested all 4,096 subsets and confirmed counts 16,72,129,116,54,12,1, 400 total, 16 minima, the same 24 jump and slide edges, diameter 4, and degree multiplicities 9,6,1 at degrees 2,4,6.
residual_risks: This is a single-edge, unweighted result for GP(6,2); it does not extend by the same argument to general Petersen graphs or to reconfiguration of nonminimum sets.

value.rationale: The canonical cubic polyhedral graph has short cycles and diameter four, outside the cited simple cover criteria. The exact answer replaces a list of subsets by independent parity constraints, explains why every minimal solution is optimal, and determines the entire optimal motion space, including why restricting to slides costs no moves. These answer concrete questions about this standard graph that the minimum number alone cannot answer.
residual_risks: The contribution is a narrow exact invariant of one standard graph, not a general theory of MEG reconfiguration.
